+        # per token id, so merges can use str.split (non-overlapping, left to
+        # right, exactly like merge()). the chunks are joined by a separator
+        # code point that is never a token id, so no pair crosses a chunk

+            for p0, nexts in lookup.items():
+                table[p0] = nexts
+            self._merge_table = table
+            self._merge_table_src = lookup

+        # return the token ids
+        # let's begin. first, convert all bytes to integers in range 0..255
+        ids = list(text_bytes)
+        if type(merge_lookup) is not list:
+            merge_lookup = self._get_merge_table()
+        while len(ids) >= 2:
+            # find the pair with the lowest merge index
+            best_idx = None
+            it = iter(ids)
+            prev = next(it)
+            for curr in it:
+                nexts = merge_lookup[prev]
+                if nexts is not None:
+                    idx = nexts.get(curr)
+                    if idx is not None:
+                        if best_idx is None or idx < best_idx:
+                            best_p0 = prev
+                            best_p1 = curr
+                            best_idx = idx
+                            repeated = False
+                        elif prev == best_p0 and curr == best_p1:
+                            repeated = True
+                prev = curr
+            if best_idx is None:
+                break # nothing else can be merged anymore
+            if not repeated:

+                i = ids.index(best_p0)
+                while ids[i+1] != best_p1:
+                    i = ids.index(best_p0, i + 1)
+                ids[i:i+2] = [best_idx]

+            append = newids.append
+            i = 0
+            n = len(ids)
+            last = n - 1

+                if ids[i] == best_p0 and ids[i+1] == best_p1:
+                    append(best_idx)
+                    i += 2
+                else:
+                    append(ids[i])
+                    i += 1
+            if i == last:
+                append(ids[i])

+        # merges are unchanged (the cache is reset whenever the lookup is)

+        allowed_special: can be "all"|"none"|"none_raise" or a custom set of special tokens
+        if none_raise, then an error is raised if any special token is encountered in text
+        this is the default tiktoken behavior right now as well
+        any other behavior is either annoying, or a major footgun
+        """
+        # decode the user desire w.r.t. handling of special tokens
+        special = None
+        if allowed_special == "all":
+            special = self.special_tokens
+        elif allowed_special == "none":
+            special = {}
+        elif allowed_special == "none_raise":
+            special = {}
+            assert all(token not in text for token in self.special_tokens)
+        elif isinstance(allowed_special, set):
+            special = {k: v for k, v in self.special_tokens.items() if k in allowed_special}
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"allowed_special={allowed_special} not understood")
+        if not special:
+            # shortcut: if no special tokens, just use the ordinary encoding
+            return self.encode_ordinary(text)
+        # otherwise, we have to be careful with potential special tokens in text
+        if all(type(k) is str and k for k in special):
+            # split at the leftmost occurrence of any special token (the first
+            # listed one on a tie), which is what the alternation below matches
+            ids = []
+            start = 0
+            while True:
+                pos = -1
+                for k in special:
+                    j = text.find(k, start)
+                    if j != -1 and (pos == -1 or j < pos):
+                        pos = j
+                        tok = k
+                if pos == -1:
+                    break
+                ids.extend(self.encode_ordinary(text[start:pos]))
+                ids.append(special[tok])
+                start = pos + len(tok)
+            ids.extend(self.encode_ordinary(text[start:]))
+            return ids

+        # based on the occurrence of any exact match with any of the special tokens
+        # we can use re.split for this. note that surrounding the pattern with ()
+        # makes it into a capturing group, so the special tokens will be included

+        # all chunks of text are encoded separately, then results are joined
+        ids = []
+        for part in special_chunks:

+                ids.append(special[part])
+            else:

+                ids.extend(self.encode_ordinary(part))

journal.text:
I worked on train_ir in minbpe/regex.py and made four attempts. The first counted the initial pair stats in C, with each chunk repeated by its count. The second trained on one joined chunk string with a separator, the way BasicTokenizer.train does. The third added a fast path for chunks with exactly one occurrence. The fourth was a 29-line variant.

The first measured ratio 1.0402 on train_ir, so it was slower. The second measured 1.1967, much slower, though encode_ir came in at 0.9918. The third changed outputs and failed 3 stable tests, including test_save_load and test_wikipedia_example[RegexTokenizer]. The fourth measured 0.9921 against the required 0.9900. That is close but did not clear it. I submitted nothing.

Working on the deduplicated chunks matters. Joining them into one string loses that benefit. Moving the initial count to C did not help.

Next I would start from the 0.9921 variant and look for the rest in the per-merge update. Any fast path must keep outputs identical.
